hook_text: March 1900: a British governor asks where the Golden Stool is, and says he should be sitting on it. The room goes silent.
clip_script: By 1872 Britain owned every fort on the coast. In 1874 its army cut a road through the forest and burned Kumasi. In the 1890s, the scramble was on, and Britain feared France or Germany would get there first. Prempeh I said no to British protection. In 1896 soldiers came; Prempeh chose not to fight, to save his people, and was exiled to islands thousands of kilometres away. Then Governor Hodgson made his demand about the Golden Stool. To the Asante, it held the soul of the nation. Yaa Asantewaa said: if the men will not fight, the women will. The Asante besieged the British fort for months. Britain won the war. It never found the stool.
visual_style: A whiteboard timeline from 1872 to 1902, a burning Kumasi, an empty throne, a fort under siege and a shadowed hidden Golden Stool.
pacing: Builds steadily to the demand, then fast through the war, ending quietly.
